entities.name: Nitro heteroarene reduction
observations: Reactant O=C1C([N+](=O)[O-])=CC(C2=CC=CC=N2)=CN1C3=CC=CC=C3 converts to amino pyridone product Nc1cc(-c2ccccn2)cn(-c2ccccc2)c1=O.
The net transformation is reduction of an aromatic nitro group to a primary amino group; the pyridone/lactam carbonyl is retained.
No separate carbonyl-forming or ring-closing event is evident in this encoded transformation.

entities.name: H2 Pd-C ethanol
observations: Closest ORD record supports catalytic hydrogenation with H2, Pd, elemental carbon consistent with Pd/C, and ethanol for nitro-to-amino conversion.
Practical conditions: H2 at approximately 1–3 atm, catalytic Pd/C, ethanol or EtOH/EtOAc, room temperature to mild heating.
